issues.failure_explanation: The abstract, introduction and conclusions claim the paper demonstrates that sigma_opt is the optimal choice among all sigma and achieves the 'theoretically optimal' rate. What is actually proved (Theorems 1.1, 1.2, 4.1) are existence results giving upper bounds only: at sigma_opt the error is O(e^{-pi*sqrt(2(2-beta)N alpha)}), and for sigma != sigma_opt the proven upper bounds are worse. No lower bound is proved anywhere: nothing rules out that some other sigma (or another scheme) attains the same or faster convergence; and for beta in (0,2) even optimality of the rate e^{-pi*sqrt(2(2-beta)N alpha)} itself is unestablished (only at beta=0 does it match Stahl's sharp rate for degree-N rational approximation of x^alpha, which does give genuine optimality there).

failure_location.quote: and demonstrate that the choice $\sigma_{\mathrm{opt}} =\frac{\sqrt{2(2 - \beta)}\pi}{\sqrt{\alpha}}$ achieves the theoretically optimal convergence rate $\mathcal{O}\left(e^{-\sqrt{2(2 - \beta)N\alpha}\pi}\right)$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Weaken the prose to what is proved (sigma_opt gives the best rate among the established upper bounds, and at beta=0 the rate matches Stahl's optimal rational rate), or supply lower bounds showing that no LP with sigma != sigma_opt attains the sigma_opt-rate.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised guarantee that sigma_opt provably yields the fastest rate among all sigma>0 (and that the rate is 'theoretically optimal' for beta>0) is unreliable. The formal upper-bound results and the confirmation of Conjectures 1.1/1.2 are not affected.
issues.title: Optimality of sigma_opt among all clustering parameters is asserted but never established
issues.why_classification: Preserving the optimality claim as stated requires new lower-bound results; weakening it abandons an advertised (beta>0) optimality guarantee while leaving all formal results intact - a limited weakening with recognizably comparable content, hence moderate.

issues.failure_explanation: Omega_rho is the disk |z|<=1+d minus the notch {z=-d+x e^{+/- i theta pi/2}: 0<=x<=1, beta<=theta<=2}. At beta=0 the directions theta in [0,2] cover all angles, so the removed notch is the full closed disk of radius 1 about -d, which contains the segment [0,1-d] of S_0=[0,1] (e.g. z=1/2 = -d+(d+1/2)e^{i0} with theta=0). Hence Omega_rho does not contain S_0, contradicting the asserted property 'Omega_rho superset S_beta'. The Walsh-Hermite representation of r_2-q_n is invoked for z in S_beta but is valid only for z inside the contour Gamma_rho = boundary(Omega_rho); for z in [0,1-d] it is invalid, so the polynomial-approximation estimates (2.31)-(2.32), and with them the proofs of Theorems 1.1/1.2 in the beta=0 case (Conjecture 1.1, the Stahl comparison), are not established as written. For beta in (0,2) a triangle-angle argument shows S_beta avoids the notch, so the failure is exactly at beta=0, a regime explicitly in scope (cf. (2.10)).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: For beta=0 replace Omega_rho by a suitable neighborhood of [0,1] that avoids the poles (e.g. a tube of radius eps<C/2 around [0,1], or the Omega_rho associated with a fixed beta_0>0), verify r_2's analyticity and the |Ce^{t/alpha}+z| and product bounds there, and rerun the Hermite/Fekete argument; all rates and the beta=0 scope are preserved.
issues.overall_effect: The N_2=O(sqrt(N_1)) polynomial-approximation step of the construction is unjustified on [0,1-d] at beta=0, leaving Theorems 1.1/1.2 (and Corollary 1.3, Theorem 4.1 at beta=0), including the claimed proof of Conjecture 1.1, with a proof gap in that regime.
issues.title: Auxiliary domain Omega_rho fails to contain S_beta at beta=0, breaking the Runge/Hermite step
issues.why_classification: A degenerate-case (beta=0) failure of a load-bearing construction whose repair needs a new auxiliary domain and re-derivation of several uniform estimates - contained, with no loss of rates or scope, but more than a routine local edit.

Since (2.28), the bound on ||r_2||_{C(Omega_rho)}, is derived term-by-term from this denominator estimate, the r_2-bound, the polynomial-approximation error (2.31) and the reduction to N_2=O(sqrt(N_1)) are not established as written.

issues.failure_explanation: The corollary asserts that r_N(x^2) (and r_tilde_N(x^2)) has 'tapered lightning poles (2.13)', i.e. the N_1 points i*sqrt(C)e^{-(sigma/2)(sqrt(N_1)-sqrt(j))}. Composing the LP (1.1), the poles in x satisfy x^2=p_j, i.e. x = +/- i*sqrt(C)e^{-(sigma/2)(sqrt(N_1)-sqrt(j))}: both signs, 2N_1 poles with opposite residues. The stated one-signed pole set is therefore wrong: an LP built with only the (2.13) poles would not equal r_N(x^2) and the stated guarantees would not apply to it. The error bounds (2.14)-(2.15) themselves are correct for r_N(x^2).

issues.failure_explanation: In Case 2 of the proof of Theorem 3.4, display (3.35) collapses the Poisson sum to O(T^l e^{-T}). Its second term is 1/(e^{(4 pi^2 alpha/h)(T+alpha log(delta/C))}-1) with 4 pi^2 alpha/h = (2/(2-beta)) eta^2; for sigma>sigma_opt (eta<1) this term decays like e^{-eta^2 (T+...)}, which is slower than e^{-T} whenever (2/(2-beta))eta^2<1 (in particular for every sigma>sigma_opt when beta=0). The paper's own preceding step, via Lemma 3.3, gives O(e^{-eta^2 T}) for the s_pole residue sum in this regime, so the asserted O(T^l e^{-T}) contradicts it. The theorem's final claim (3.9) still follows, since its sigma>sigma_opt branch is the weaker O(e^{-pi eta sqrt(2(2-beta)N alpha)}), but the proof must retain the case split.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Keep the case split from Lemma 3.3 in (3.35) (O(T^l e^{-T}) for sigma<=sigma_opt, O(e^{-eta^2 T}) for sigma>sigma_opt) and observe that both imply (3.9); no conclusion changes.
issues.overall_effect: A false intermediate rate claim inside the proof of Theorem 3.4; no stated theorem or downstream result is invalidated, since Theorems 1.1/1.2 use only (3.9), which survives.

issues.failure_explanation: Theorem 4.1 sets sigma_opt = 2 sqrt(2-beta) pi / sqrt(alpha), whereas Theorem 1.1, Conjecture 1.2 (1.11), (5.10) and Section 5 all use sigma_opt = pi sqrt(2(2-beta))/sqrt(alpha), which is smaller by a factor sqrt(2). With the inflated value the first branch is asserted up to sigma = sqrt(2) sigma_opt, and the second branch's rate O(e^{-pi eta sqrt(2(2-beta)N alpha)}) uses eta inflated by sqrt(2), i.e. exponents sqrt(2) times larger than what (4.1)-(4.2) establish (and, per the paper's own analysis and Fig. 2, faster than actually holds under over-clustering); the two branches are also discontinuous at the stated sigma_opt. The proof derives (4.7)-(4.9) solely from Theorems 1.1/1.2 (which use the correct sigma_opt) and never uses the stated value; moreover beta is never quantified in the statement. As written, Theorem 4.1 asserts stronger convergence guarantees than are proven.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct sigma_opt in Theorem 4.1 to pi sqrt(2(2-beta))/sqrt(alpha) (and quantify beta in [0,2) among the hypotheses); the existing proof then matches the statement.
issues.overall_effect: The statement of Theorem 4.1 is false as written in the over-clustering regime sigma>sigma_opt; nothing downstream is invalidated, since Theorem 5.1 invokes it only with sigma = pi sqrt(2(2-beta))/sqrt(alpha), the first-branch part that remains established.
issues.title: Theorem 4.1 states sigma_opt = 2 pi sqrt(2-beta)/sqrt(alpha), a factor sqrt(2) larger than the value used elsewhere, asserting unproven rates
